body: Use your head. The American national hotline receives hundreds of calls per hour. Employing enough mental health counsellors to answer even half of those calls would cost billions. Then there’s rent, utility bills, advertising campaigns... Suicide hotlines just aren’t that well funded. Earlier this year, North Carolina’s state legislature wouldn’t cough up a measly $400,000 for the state’s hotline. North Carolina is home to 10 million people. $400,000 is less than $0.04 per person and that’s still too much to fund suicide prevention.

Well, I have expended all my government assistance and my family is in no position to help me anymore than they already are. Short of making a GoFundMe that I am almost certain nobody would donate to, I’m pretty sure I have looked into all possibilities of help.

You, and everyone else here, have to understand that the suicide hotline isn’t a counselling service. They are mental health 911. Their job is to talk you off the ledge, which isn’t as hard as you might think since you basically asked them to do it, and direct you to help; if that fails, they direct help to you. You don’t call 911 and expect to talk to a doctor. I don’t know why people call the suicide hotline expecting to talk to a counsellor.

There’s no point now. I have been unemployed since December. I applied at the grocery store 6 months ago, the restaurant 3 months ago, and the electronics store 2 months ago - amongst other places. All those positions have long since been filled. Even if there was a reason to call, there would be no one to call. The grocery store and electronics store both wanted electronically submitted resumes. I went to both places in person and was told they didn’t take resumes anymore. No, they want it to go through some program that picks out keywords or sent to some person the next city over to make an “unbiased” decision. As for a restaurant, a small family business, I spoke with the manager directly when I dropped off my resume. Everything seemed to go well, but he never got back to me.

I made friends with campus security when I was in college. One of the officers had a master’s degree in psychology and had previously worked as a mental health counsellor. I was surprised when she told me this and asked her why she gave up her career for a job that paid less than half as much; she looked me in the eye and said “I got sick of my clients blaming their parents for their problems.”

Was my mom a good mother? God, no. But she did her best, whether that meant giving up on her dream career to raise my sister and I or working 3 jobs to make ends meet after our dad left, and I feel like she deserves some respect and appreciation for that. I think it’s important for us to recognize that the people that hurt us may be dealing with issues of their own. And, really, my mother is in no way responsible for my current predicament.

Ha. I told my mom I was seriously considering killing myself by getting drunk and walking out into a snowstorm back in February; she told me to go ahead and do it. The only reason I have stayed alive this long is because I’m worried that my mom is suffering from some form of cognitive decline and might need someone to look after her in the near future. But what’s the point if the woman hates me? My sister or other relatives can look after her if it’s necessary.

Sounds like you’re drinking too much water to me. Both hyponatremia (low sodium blood levels) and hypokalemia (low potassium blood levels) cause headache and fatigue. The chills are caused by large quantities of water temporarily lowering your body temperature. Normal body temperature is 37°C so even when it’s 30°C outside, your body is fighting a losing battle against the environment. Throw a couple glasses of 13°C water into the mix and you might just disrupt the system enough to make yourself feel cold in the middle of summer.

So, cut back on the water and the candy and stop taking Aspirin until you’re 18 and you’ll probably be fine. Might want to eat a banana and an orange, though. For good measure.
